questions.prompt: Which approach best supports reliable work with Logging and Monitoring?
options: Assume every supported runtime has identical APIs and scheduling behavior.
Store credentials and production secrets directly in the source file.
Keep secrets in the deployment environment, provide health checks, and stop accepting new work before draining in-flight work.
Skip input validation because Node.js applications run on a trusted server.
questions.answer_key: Keep secrets in the deployment environment, provide health checks, and stop accepting new work before draining in-flight work.
questions.explanation: Keep secrets in the deployment environment, provide health checks, and stop accepting new work before draining in-flight work. The example and verification steps should make this practice observable.

questions.prompt: Which topic is explicitly listed under Logging and Monitoring?
questions.explanation: “Structured logs” is one of the subtopics retained from the supplied Node.js curriculum for this lesson.

questions.prompt: Before relying on a Logging and Monitoring implementation, what verification is most useful?
options: Verify the documented result in a supported runtime and test one failure or boundary case.
Assume the API behaves as expected without running a check.
Ignore failures so the program continues silently.
Use the same code regardless of documented version differences.
questions.answer_key: Verify the documented result in a supported runtime and test one failure or boundary case.
questions.explanation: A small deterministic check plus a failure/boundary case helps distinguish a correct design from a happy-path-only example.
